newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei ends up on Dow, machinery orders.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei ends up on Dow, machinery orders.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended slightly higher on Monday, partly reversing a weaker trend at the end of last week on the back of Friday's U.S. stockmarket rally and on positive economic news.
Dealers said the benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract, which closed 50 points higher at 21,200 on Monday, looked set for further gains on Tuesday.
Volume for the December contract was a low 9,170 lots.
"The stronger Dow (Jones Industrial Average) in New York now appears to be underpinning the Nikkei," said a Japanese dealer, adding. "It is also being helped by good economic figures."
He referred to an industry report earlier on Monday showing industrial machinery orders were up 27 percent in August year-on-year.

Another dealer said Monday's firmer close looked positive to chart analysts, suggesting the December contract would rise again on Tuesday. "With this close, I think we can see a slightly higher move tomorrow -- maybe towards 21,350," he said.
But he warned the upward trend was still not unbreakable.
"If we move down out of this range, to close under 21,000, then we are into a new lower range and aren't likely to find much support until 20,050," he said.
